rendered:
The document doesn't give a blind-test accuracy for the ternary bacterial mixtures. The only blind tests it describes were on single strains at unknown concentrations: "Blind tests were performed on four strains at unknown concentrations, which delivered 100% classification accuracy[1]" (Supplementary Tables S9–S12). These come from the concentration section, before the section on mixed samples.

For the mixtures, the paper only reports results qualitatively. It studied binary mixtures (A +B) and ternary mixtures (A +B +C)[2] at an equal compositional ratio and says that "the multicomponent bacterial mixtures could also be effectively classified[3]", based on the LDA score plots in Fig. 4[4] (panels d–f) and the supplementary figures. It gives no blind test or accuracy percentage for these mixtures.
